section_summary.extract_value: This convergent validity section reports that absolute breast size dissatisfaction was calculated (M = 2.88, SD = 2.16) and bivariate correlations were computed (see Table 1). Greater breast size dissatisfaction was significantly associated with higher BMI, lower body appreciation and body satisfaction, and several sociocultural appearance variables; supplementary analyses restricted to women who desired larger breasts yielded consistent results. There is no mention of 'Study 1', 'Experiment 2', or multiple studies in the provided text.
section_summary.evidence_source: Quoted sentences from provided text: 'We calculated absolute (unsigned) breast size dissatisfaction for further analyses, such that higher scores reflect greater breast size dissatisfaction (M = 2.88, SD = 2.16).'; 'Bivariate correlations were computed between this score and all additional variables.'; 'As seen in Table 1, greater breast size dissatisfaction was significantly associated with greater weight discrepancy, higher BMI, lower body appreciation, lower body satisfaction, greater use of information from society about appearance ideals, greater perceived pressure from society about appearance ideals, and greater internalisation of general and athletic appearance ideals, respectively.'; 'additional analyses only with women who desired larger breasts were conducted (reported as Supplementary Materials) and were consistent with the findings reported for the total sample.'
